questions.question: Why should an error reply contain a stable code such as PRODUCT_NOT_FOUND as well as a message?
options: Because programs need a value that does not change when the message text is reworded
Because Spring Boot requires a code field
Because codes make the reply shorter than the HTTP status
questions.explanation: Client code can branch on the code safely, while the message is written for people and may be changed.

questions.question: Which RFC defines the standard Problem Details format that Spring supports through ProblemDetail?
questions.explanation: RFC 9457 defines Problem Details for HTTP APIs, with the fields type, title, status, detail and instance.

questions.question: The FreshCart ApiError uses @JsonInclude(NON_EMPTY). For a missing product, the handler passes an empty list of field issues. Which key is missing from the JSON?
questions.explanation: NON_EMPTY leaves out empty values, so fieldErrors does not appear when the list is empty.

questions.question: A client sends DELETE /products/1, which allows only GET. The advice has a catch-all Exception handler and no handler for framework exceptions. Which status does the client receive?
questions.explanation: The catch-all handler swallows the method-not-supported exception and turns it into a 500 error.

questions.question: A team writes one advice returning ApiError and another returning a plain Map for a few endpoints. What problem does this create?
options: Clients need different parsers for different errors
questions.explanation: Mixed shapes defeat the purpose of a standard error response, because clients cannot rely on one layout.
